title: GPX Waypoint Count Tool: Standalone Waypoints
description: Count standalone waypoint elements in a GPX file with the GPX Waypoint Count Tool — saved places tallied locally, trackpoints excluded. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a geocacher's file might hold 250 standalone waypoints and zero tracks — a count this tool reports exactly, where track-focused tools would misleadingly say the file is empty.
quick_answer: The GPX Waypoint Count Tool counts the standalone <wpt> elements in a GPX file — the saved places, trailheads and caches stored outside any track or route. Drop the file and read the waypoint count locally; trackpoints and route points are counted by their own tools, never mixed in here.

faq: Why is my count zero for a full recording?
Because recordings store trackpoints, not waypoints. Zero here plus thousands in the total counter is the normal signature of a device-recorded file.
Do route points count as waypoints?
No — <rtept> belongs to a route's sequence. This tool counts only standalone <wpt> elements, the file's free-standing saved places.
Geocache files with huge waypoint counts?
Pocket queries commonly hold 500–1,000 waypoints plus child points (parking, stages) as additional wpt entries — the count reflects the file, not the cache count.
Varies by model — handhelds often cap waypoints in the low thousands. Counting before a bulk load prevents the silent truncation devices perform at the limit.
Can I extract the waypoints to a list?
The viewer shows them; extraction to CSV rides the GPX to CSV Converter, which flattens points including wpt entries.
They are ordinary <wpt> elements with conventional name prefixes — counted like all others, which is why cache files count higher than cache numbers.
It counts — and it usually marks a data-entry accident (the Gulf of Guinea collects default coordinates from every ecosystem).
